official_questions.stem: The Article 243-G of the Indian Constitution contains:

official_questions.key: The powers and functions of Village Panchayats
official_questions.core_fact: Article 243G: powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (economic development, social justice, Eleventh Schedule's 29 subjects); 243H = taxes and funds; 243I = State Finance Commission.

statements.t: Article 243-G of the Constitution contains The financial resources of Panchayat Raj Bodies.
statements.fact: Financial resources (taxes, grants, funds) are in Article 243H (and 243I SFC).

statements.t: Article 243-G of the Constitution contains The functions of the Nyaya Panchayats.
statements.fact: Part IX has no article on Nyaya Panchayats (they are State-law bodies).

statements.t: Article 243-G of the Constitution contains The powers and functions of Village Panchayats.
Article 243-G of the Constitution contains The powers of chairpersons of Zilla Parishads and Mandal Parishads.

official_questions.rule: 243B three tiers, 243C composition/chairpersons, 243D reservation, 243E term, 243G powers, 243H taxes, 243I SFC, 243K SEC.
official_questions.key_note: Key's wording 'Village Panchayats' is loose: 243G covers Panchayats at all levels.

official_questions.stem:
The powers of the Election Commission include which of the following ?
I. The Election Commission takes decisions on every aspect of conduct and control of elections from the announcement of elections to the declaration of results.
II. During the election period, the Election Commission can order the Government to dismiss some government officials.
III. When on election duty, Government officers work under the control of the Election Commission.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 324: ECI superintends, directs and controls elections from notification to results; officers on election duty are deemed on deputation to the ECI (RPA 1951 s.13CC); it can recommend transfer/suspension or disciplinary action but cannot order dismissal.

statements.t: The ECI decides every aspect of conduct and control of elections from announcement to results.
statements.d: every aspect of conduct and control

statements.t: During elections the ECI can order the government to dismiss some officials.
statements.fact: ECI can seek transfer/suspension or disciplinary action, not order dismissal.

statements.t: When on election duty, government officers work under the control of the ECI.
statements.d: work under the control of the Election Commission

official_questions.rule: ECI: transfer/suspend/recommend action – not dismiss; officials deemed on deputation during polls.

official_questions.stem:
What is/are the provision(s) to safeguard the autonomy of the Supreme Court of India ?
I. While appointing the Supreme Court Judges, the President of India has to consult the Chief Justice of India.
II. The Supreme Court Judges can be removed by the Chief Justice of India only.
III. The salaries of the Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India on which the legislature does not have to vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: Safeguards: consultation with CJI in appointments (Art. 124(2)); salaries charged on Consolidated Fund (Art. 112(3)(d)); removal only by President after Parliament's special-majority address (Art. 124(4)).

statements.t: While appointing SC judges the President has to consult the CJI.
statements.d: consult the Chief Justice of India

statements.t: SC judges can be removed by the CJI only.
statements.d: removed by the Chief Justice of India
statements.fact: Judges are removed by the President on an address of both Houses (Art. 124(4)), not by the CJI.

statements.t: Judges' salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and not voted by the legislature.

official_questions.rule: SC independence: charged expenditure, security of tenure (Art. 124(4)), no post-retirement practice in India, salaries not reduced (except financial emergency).

official_questions.core_fact: Art. 131: disputes between GoI and States, GoI+States vs States, and between States; Parliament/Assembly election disputes go to High Courts (RPA 1951); GoI-UT disputes are not federal disputes.

statements.t: A dispute between two or more States falls within the SC's original jurisdiction.
A dispute regarding elections to Parliament or State legislatures falls within the SC's original jurisdiction.
statements.d: elections to either House of the Parliament
statements.fact: Election petitions for Parliament/State legislatures are tried by High Courts (RPA 1951); only President/VP election disputes go to the SC (Art. 71).

statements.t: A dispute between the GoI and a Union Territory falls within the SC's original jurisdiction.
statements.fact: Art. 131 covers Centre-State and inter-State disputes, not Centre-UT disputes.

statements.t: A dispute between the GoI and one or more States falls within the SC's original jurisdiction.
statements.d: Government of India and one or more States

official_questions.rule: Art. 131 = federal disputes only; election petitions -> HC; President/VP -> SC (Art. 71).

official_questions.rule: Reports to President: NCSC, NCST, NCBC, CAG (Union), UPSC, FC; to Governor: SPSC, CAG (State).

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not a function of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) ?
options: Conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 320: UPSC conducts examinations, is consulted on recruitment methods, promotions/transfers suitability, disciplinary matters; Art. 320(4): not consulted on reservation of posts for backward classes (Art. 16(4)) or claims of SC/ST (Art. 335).

statements.t: The UPSC conducts examinations for appointments to Union services.
The UPSC is consulted on disciplinary matters.
The UPSC is consulted on methods of recruitment.
The UPSC is consulted on the manner of reservation of posts.
statements.fact: Art. 320(4) excludes reservation of posts from UPSC consultation.

official_questions.rule: UPSC not consulted on: reservation (16(4)), SC/ST claims (335), certain posts exempted by President's regulations.
official_questions.key_note: Initial key only. 'All disciplinary matters' is loose: it is disciplinary matters affecting civil servants.

official_questions.core_fact: Eleventh Schedule includes women and child development (25), public distribution system (28), libraries (20), markets and fairs (22); slum improvement and upgradation is Twelfth Schedule item 10 (municipalities).

statements.t: Women and child development is listed in the Eleventh Schedule.
Public distribution system is listed in the Eleventh Schedule.
Libraries are listed in the Eleventh Schedule.
Slum improvement and upgradation is listed in the Eleventh Schedule.

official_questions.stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 :
I. The Act empowers authorities like the Director to attach property believed to be “proceeds of crime”.
II. Offences under Part A of the Schedule deal with trans-border crimes and reflect the dedication to tackle money laundering across the global boundaries.
III. The Act and the Rules notified thereunder came into force with effect from 2005.
IV. The Act has provided for an Appellate Tribunal and Special Court to conduct the trial of the offences of money laundering.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: PMLA 2002 (in force 1 July 2005) lets the Director (ED) provisionally attach proceeds of crime (s.5); the Schedule has Part A (listed offences), Part B (Customs Act s.132 offences) and Part C (offences with cross-border implications); it provides an Adjudicating Authority, Appellate Tribunal and Special Courts.

statements.t: PMLA empowers the Director to attach property believed to be proceeds of crime.
Offences under Part A of the PMLA Schedule deal with trans-border crimes.
statements.fact: Part C of the Schedule covers offences of cross-border implications; Part A lists ordinary scheduled offences.

statements.t: PMLA and its Rules came into force with effect from 2005.
PMLA provides for an Appellate Tribunal and Special Courts to try money-laundering offences.

official_questions.rule: PMLA Schedule: A = listed offences, B = Customs s.132, C = cross-border; Act 2002, in force 2005.
official_questions.key_note: App explanation says Part B; per the Act it is Part C that covers cross-border offences. Key unaffected.

official_questions.stem:
Consider the following statements in connection with the office of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) :
I. CAG can be removed by the President only in accordance with the procedure mentioned in the Constitution but this does not mean that the CAG can be impeached from office in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
II. Some public corporations are audited exclusively by private professional auditors, and the CAG may have no involvement at all.
III. The CAG can conduct legal, regulatory and propriety audit but not performance audit.
IV. The Constitution of India has not specified any criterion for the appointment of CAG.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 148(1): CAG removed only in like manner and on like grounds as an SC judge; some corporations are audited solely by private auditors (no CAG role); CAG does legal, regulatory, propriety and (discretionary) performance audits; Constitution prescribes no qualifications.

statements.t: The CAG can be removed only per the Constitution, but this does not mean removal in the same manner as an SC judge.
statements.d: does not mean ... same manner as a Judge
statements.fact: The CAG is removed in the same manner as an SC judge (Art. 148(1)).

statements.t: Some public corporations are audited exclusively by private auditors with no CAG involvement.
statements.d: audited exclusively by private professional auditors

statements.t: The CAG can conduct legal, regulatory and propriety audit but not performance audit.
statements.fact: The CAG also conducts performance (efficiency/economy) audits.

statements.t: The Constitution has not specified any criterion for appointment of the CAG.

official_questions.rule: CAG: removal like SC judge, 6 years/65, no qualifications; audits: legal/regulatory (mandatory), propriety/performance (discretionary).

official_questions.stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Election Commission of India :
I. The Constitution of India has debarred the retiring Election Commissioners from any further appointment by the government.
II. In 'Anoop Baranwal Case' (2023), the Supreme Court has directed the Government to treat the Regional Commissioners on par with the Election Commissioners (other than the Chief Election Commissioner), as far as removal from office is concerned.
III. Since its inception, the Election Commission had functioned as a multi-member body.
IV. The power of superintendence, direction and control of elections to the office of Vice-President of India is vested in the Election Commission.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 324: ECI controls elections to Parliament, State legislatures, President and Vice-President; Constitution does not bar retiring ECs from later posts; ECI was single-member till Oct 1989 (multi-member again from 1993); Art. 324(5) proviso protects Regional Commissioners' removal (recommendation of CEC) – Anoop Baranwal (2023) concerned appointment of CEC/ECs.

statements.t: The Constitution debars retiring Election Commissioners from further government appointment.
statements.fact: The Constitution does not bar retiring ECs from further government appointment (a noted weakness).

statements.t: In Anoop Baranwal (2023) the SC directed that Regional Commissioners be treated on par with ECs for removal.
statements.fact: Anoop Baranwal (2023) set a PM-LoP-CJI selection committee for appointments; Regional Commissioners' removal protection is in Art. 324(5) itself.

statements.t: Since its inception the ECI has functioned as a multi-member body.
statements.fact: The ECI was single-member from 1950 to 1989 (and 1990-93).

statements.t: Superintendence, direction and control of the Vice-Presidential election is vested in the ECI.

official_questions.rule: ECI: Art. 324 – Parliament, States, President, VP (not local bodies, which SECs conduct); multi-member permanent since 1993; 2023 Act: selection committee PM + LoP + Cabinet Minister.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statement/statements can be attributed correctly to the exercise of Delimitation ?
I. The principle of 'one man, one vote' reiterates the need for the exercise of Delimitation.
II. The Government of India can set up a Delimitation Commission for the purpose of delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies in a select few States or UTs.
III. The Delimitation Commission can only recommend the re-delimitation of territorial Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies but cannot recommend on the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
IV. The Nodal Ministry for the Delimitation Commission of India is the Ministry of Law and Justice.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
official_questions.core_fact: Delimitation implements 'one person, one vote, one value'; the Centre can set up a Commission for select States/UTs (2020: J&K and 4 NE States); the Commission also identifies seats reserved for SCs/STs; its orders cannot be challenged in court; nodal ministry: Law and Justice (Legislative Department).

statements.t: The principle of 'one man, one vote' underlines the need for delimitation.
The GoI can set up a Delimitation Commission for select States or UTs.
The Delimitation Commission cannot recommend on reservation of seats for SCs and STs.
statements.fact: The Commission also determines seats reserved for SCs and STs.

statements.t: The nodal ministry for the Delimitation Commission is the Ministry of Law and Justice.

official_questions.rule: Delimitation Commissions: 1952, 1963, 1973, 2002 (2001 census); orders final, not questionable in court; freeze till first census after 2026.

official_questions.stem:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : In connection with their own resource collection, the Panchayats at the village level are better placed than the Panchayats at the Intermediate and the District levels.
Reason (R) : The Gram Panchayats have their own tax domain whereas the other two tiers have to depend only on tolls, fees and non-tax revenue for internal resource generation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
official_questions.key: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) explains (A).
official_questions.core_fact: In most State Panchayat Acts only Gram Panchayats get a real tax domain (house/property tax, profession tax); intermediate and district Panchayats rely on tolls, fees, non-tax revenue and grants.

statements.t: Village Panchayats are better placed for own resource collection than intermediate and district Panchayats.
Gram Panchayats have their own tax domain whereas the other tiers rely on tolls, fees and non-tax revenue.
R explains A.

official_questions.rule: Own-source revenue is concentrated at the village tier; upper tiers depend on grants.
official_questions.key_note: Initial key only. 'Only' in R is a generalisation across State laws.
